name: Mango Lassi
cuisine: Punjabi / North Indian sweet yoghurt drink, sold at Mumbai lassi shops and dairies

ingredients.name: Ripe mango (aam), Alphonso, Kesar or Totapuri, or canned mango pulp
ingredients.householdMeasure: about ½ cup chopped, or ½ cup pulp

equipment: Blender or mixer-grinder jar: gives a smooth, frothy drink in about 40 seconds
Kitchen scale, measuring spoons and cup
Knife and chopping board (skip if using canned pulp)

steps.title: Peel the mango
steps.text: Wash the mango and cut off the skin with a knife, or slice the cheeks off and scoop the flesh with a spoon. No mango: open a tin of pulp and measure 100 g.
steps.visualCue: Bright orange-yellow flesh, a sweet mango smell, and juice on the board.
steps.cameraCheck: The peeled mango on the board
steps.videoShot: Knife slicing the cheek of a ripe mango.
steps.watchOut: Fibrous or sour mango, which makes a stringy or tangy lassi; taste a small piece first, and if it is sour plan for the full 10 g sugar and strain later.

steps.title: Weigh the mango
steps.text: Cut the flesh into chunks and weigh out 120 g into the blender jar.
steps.visualCue: A small heap of orange chunks, roughly ½ cup, in the jar.
steps.cameraCheck: The scale showing 120 g in the jar
steps.videoShot: Mango chunks dropping into the jar.
steps.watchOut: Adding the stone or the fibrous skin-side flesh, which stays stringy after blending; cut only the soft flesh.

steps.title: Add the curd
steps.text: Add 100 g cold curd to the jar.
steps.visualCue: A thick white blob sits on the orange chunks.
steps.cameraCheck: The curd in the measuring cup
steps.videoShot: Spoon dropping curd onto the mango.
steps.watchOut: Sour (old) curd, which makes the whole drink tangy; smell it first, and if it is sharp add 5 g more sugar later or use fresher curd.

steps.title: Add milk, sugar and cardamom
steps.text: Add 50 ml cold milk, 10 g sugar (2 tsp) and a pinch (0.3 g) of cardamom powder.
steps.visualCue: Everything sits in layers; the cardamom smells sweet and floral.
steps.cameraCheck: The jar with all ingredients layered
steps.videoShot: Sugar and cardamom falling on the curd.
steps.watchOut: Too much cardamom, which tastes soapy; use only a small pinch.

steps.title: Add the ice
steps.visualCue: Three clear cubes on top of the mixture.
steps.watchOut: Too much ice, which thins the lassi as it melts into a watery drink; stay at 3 cubes.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Close the lid and blend on high for 40 to 60 seconds.
steps.visualCue: The mix turns one even pale-orange colour with a light froth on top and no visible mango chunks or ice clinks.
steps.cameraCheck: The jar showing the smooth pale-orange liquid
steps.videoShot: Jar spinning to a smooth frothy blend.
steps.watchOut: Leftover lumps or ice from blending too briefly (blend 20 sec more), or a runny drink from too long blending with the ice melting (stop at 60 sec).

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.text: Dip a clean spoon in and taste. Add 1 tsp sugar and blend 10 sec if it is not sweet enough, or 1 tbsp milk if it is too thick.
steps.tip: If the mango was stringy, pour the lassi through a steel sieve into the glass.
steps.visualCue: A thick, pourable drink that coats the back of the spoon and tastes sweet with a mild tang.
steps.videoShot: Spoon lifting a ribbon of lassi from the jar.
steps.watchOut: Over-sweetening; add sugar a little at a time, since the mango itself is sweet.

steps.title: Pour and serve
steps.text: Pour into a tall glass and serve at once, cold.
steps.visualCue: A pale-orange, frothy glass that fills to about 250 ml.
steps.watchOut: Letting it stand for a long time, since the froth drops and the ice thins it; drink within 15 minutes, or stir and chill.

reasons: a short ingredient list of real fruit and curd, with calcium, vitamin C, vitamin A, B12 and little sodium (about 70 mg) and no fried or processed ingredients. Points off for about 32 g sugar (10 g added, 40% of the added-sugar limit), low fibre (1.6 g) and low protein (about 6 g). Restaurant versions are often sweeter, use sweetened canned pulp, extra sugar, cream or condensed milk and larger glasses (est.).

researchRating.basis: a very widely published and loved mango drink, found on Cook with Manali, Indian Healthy Recipes, Indian Veggie Delight, Tarla Dalal, Tea for Turmeric, Love and Other Spices, Food Network, Saveur and Swiggy's own blog, and Swiggy reported it delivered about 1,547 mango lassis a day in a summer food-trends article (Curly Tales; snippet only). Points off because it depends heavily on mango quality and can be very sugary. Recipe-site star counts were not checked this run.

storage: Best drunk fresh. Fridge-safe in a closed jar for up to 1 day (est.; not confirmed from a source); stir or shake before drinking, since it separates. Freezing: not recommended as a drink (it splits when thawed), but it can be frozen in ice-cube trays and re-blended (est.). Do not reheat.
leftoverRemix: Mango lassi popsicles. Pour leftover lassi into a lolly mould or small cups, insert a stick and freeze for 4–6 hours; add a few mango chunks for a twist.
burnOff: about 2.9 km of running (205 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 4.1 km of brisk walking (about 49 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: fruit, curd and milk are commonly allowed; sugar is usually fine, and families that avoid refined sugar can use rock sugar (mishri) (assumption: the common rule set that allows fruit and dairy).

ekadashi.reason: fruit and dairy are generally allowed and there is no grain or pulse; families differ on sugar and on curd, so check your own rule set (assumption: the common rule set).

jain.reason: no roots, onion, garlic, meat, egg or honey; dairy is accepted in Jain diets.

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; a cooling, sweet iftar drink. For sehri it is light and low in protein (about 6 g), so pair it with something more filling.

jain.reason: mango, curd, milk, sugar and cardamom; no onion, garlic, potato or other root vegetable (no fresh ginger used).

vegan.reason: curd 100 g and milk 50 ml are dairy; use unsweetened soy or coconut yoghurt and plant milk (see Vegan variant).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat or egg; no fish needed.

sattvik.reason: no onion or garlic in the recipe.

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, rava, maida or hing; check that canned mango pulp lists no added thickener from wheat.

dairyFree.reason: curd and milk are the dairy; use plant yoghurt and plant milk (see Dairy-free variant).
